name: General Insurance Corporation of India
title: General Insurance Corporation of India - 540755 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Reinsurer GIC Re enters FY27 with softening pricing and new domestic reinsurers; management guides only 1-2pt combined ratio improvement and expects low single-digit growth, with a 4% obligatory share held for FY27.

triggers.label: Two new domestic reinsurers plus GIFT City IIOs
triggers.quote: there are 2 reinsurers that have been set up just prior to 1st of April. So the competition is at our doorstep.

triggers.label: April renewal pricing pressure, fire softening
triggers.quote: there were pressures were there on the pricing because of the competition, because of the capacity available.

triggers.label: Growth low single digit, combined ratio 1-2pt better
triggers.quote: we approach renewals with both underwriting discipline and to support our markets

triggers.label: Fire domestic growth to be nil at April
triggers.quote: if your question is alone in the fire segment, yes, we will not see growth on 1st April

guidance.quote: overall target that we have put for ourselves is to improve by 2% or 1% to 2% year -on-year

guidance.value: low single-digit growth likely; single-digit growth
guidance.quote: in terms of growth, you mentioned about single -digit growth, yes, as it could be single -digit growth in the current year
obligatory 4% has been declared to GIC Re. And we will have that regulatory privilege
we are giving a dividend payout of 13.25%, which is 32% -- 32.5% more than what we have given earlier

red_flags.quote: we are still holding some reserves for the business that we underwritten in those territories? Sanjay Mokashi: Yes, we are holding reserves.

summary.headline: GIC Re FY26 profit after tax rose 25.23% to INR8,392.18 crores, with combined ratio down 2.79 points to 106.02%.
summary.overview: GIC Re reported FY26 gross premium of INR44,006.74 crores, up from INR41,153.95 crores, and PAT of INR8,392.18 crores. Q4 PAT rose to INR2,254.24 crores from INR2,182.88 crores, while Q4 investment income fell to INR3,059.46 crores from INR3,903.02 crores. Management said the global market is moving from hardening to a competitive phase, with April 1 domestic renewals and January 1 international renewals showing price pressure. Management guided to a 1-2 point combined ratio improvement in FY27 and expects low single-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Accounts for 75% of FY26 gross premium (INR32,979.23 crores). Domestic combined ratio was cited at around 101-102%, an improvement of roughly 250 bps versus FY25 per an analyst's reading; property is about 30% of the domestic book.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: FY26 gross premium of INR11,027.51 crores. Motor international is shrinking due to pruning (US contract ended; Israel and Turkey proportional treaties reduced), with claims running off more slowly than premium. Property results improving since it has no long tail.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: About 83% of motor portfolio is domestic and about 60% of that domestic portion is obligatory. Domestic motor growth came from additional domestic treaties; international motor premium has degrown over three years.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: More than 99% domestic. Proportional treaties; some reserve strengthening under way, results described as fairly stable. Management is cautious on government schemes.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Q4 fire premium decline of around 20% was attributed to international portfolio; management said the quarter alone may not reflect the full year. Domestic fire will not grow at April 1 renewals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 combined ratio targeted to improve by 1-2 percentage points year-on-year; management said it would prefer to hold or improve on the FY26 106% level.
FY27 growth expected to be low single-digit; management said it would not chase premium in a soft market.
Obligatory share of 4% declared for GIC Re for FY26-27; management flagged possible glide-path pressure on obligatory share over time.
Solvency will be used for impending RBC and IFRS transitions; dividend payout raised to 13.25%, about 32.5% higher than earlier.
capex_capacity: Solvency ratio improved to 4.21 at year-end from 3.70, which management said supports capital deployment and the RBC and IFRS transitions.
Net worth excluding fair value change grew to INR51,301.27 crores from INR43,106.52 crores.
demand_pricing: April 1 domestic renewals were pressured by competition and softening fire pricing; GIC Re used reinsurance levers (proportional structures) so the first impact is borne by insurers. Contracts above a threshold were declined.
New entrants: multiple IFSC insurance offices in GIFT City and two domestic reinsurers set up just before 1 April, increasing competition.
International 1 January renewals: market in soft cycle beyond the 2023-24 hardening, with ample capital and benign cat seasons; reinsurers still holding discipline on coverage and retentions.
Crop: new 3-year tender cycle not yet in place; burn-cost model expected to be more prevalent for FY27; only 1-2 treaties concluded so far.

qa_highlights.question: How did April renewal pricing go, and do the two new domestic reinsurers affect obligatory or domestic-preferred business?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was pressured by competition and capacity, but GIC Re retained key relationships and declined contracts beyond thresholds; growth fell short of goals. Obligatory 4% is declared for FY26-27; management expects any new player to need a track record, but a glide path is possible.

qa_highlights.question: Can domestic combined ratio hold at around 101-102% in a soft market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can hold, with property (30% of book) under pressure but agriculture and health approached cautiously. The objective is a 1-2 point improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be low single digit and combined ratio improve 1-2 points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed low single-digit growth is likely. It confirmed a 1-2 point year-on-year combined ratio improvement target, with more improvement possible in foreign business.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor profitability weak despite strong growth, and what drove the Q4 fire decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic motor growth came from new treaties; international motor is degrowing after pruning (US contract, Israel and Turkey treaties), so claims are running off slower than premium. Fire Q4 decline is from international; full-year view may be overstated by a single quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for health and April fire renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Health has reserve strengthening but results are stable; more than 99% is domestic and government-scheme exposure is being handled cautiously. Domestic fire will not grow at April 1, offset by health, agriculture and domestic motor.

qa_highlights.question: Capital: will high solvency allow higher dividend, and how does the RBC transition affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stated a 13.25% payout, about 32.5% higher than earlier, and said solvency will be used toward the RBC and IFRS transitions.

risks_watch: Softening in domestic fire and international property; new domestic reinsurers and IFSC offices raising competition.
International motor claims run-off lagging premium decline, keeping motor combined ratio elevated.
Possible glide path in the obligatory share, which currently stands at 4% for FY26-27.
Crop reinsurance volumes depend on how states choose between cup-and-cap and burn-cost models under the new tender cycle.
Investment income fell sharply in Q4 (INR3,059.46 crores vs INR3,903.02 crores), reducing support to earnings.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and capital, but cautious and somewhat defensive on FY27 growth, fire pricing and motor profitability. Management repeatedly framed softer premium as deliberate discipline rather than lost business.
key_quotes: So yes, our capital solvency is very high, and we are giving a dividend payout of 13.25%, which is 32% -- 32.5% more than what we have given earlier.
It can hold up because property is 30% of our book, wherein we -- as we mentioned, that we did that balancing act and there could be pressure on the combined ratio there.
And therefore, on the international side, there is a degrowth. But the degrowth impact is immediately seen on the portfolio.

growth.why: Management guides low single-digit (possibly single-digit) premium growth for FY27 and says it will not chase premium in a softening market, with a 1-2 point combined ratio improvement targeted through underwriting discipline and reinsurance structuring rather than any capacity or order book.
